CENSUS OF ANTHONY'S FIVE PROJECTS, 2026-08-09, via `describe_designs` — which reads only the sidecar beside each store, opens nothing, takes no lock and writes nothing. READ ONLY.

  project                     graph_id                label              minted_by   stamp
  A dynograph-foundation      dynograph-foundation    dynograph-foundation  0.16.0    0.16.0  (56 edge / 28 node types)
  B reflow2                   reflow2                 reflow2               0.13.0    0.26.1  (61 / 29)
  C flo2                      1a97fc1f1de4d5d2        flo2                  0.24.0    0.26.1  (60 / 29)
  D dev_storyflow             reflow2   ⚠️            dev_storyflow         0.14.0    0.26.1  (61 / 29)
  E embeddings-rs             —                       —                     —         ABSENT

=== ✅ PROJECT E IS NOT A REFLOW2 PROJECT — the open question is answered ===

Anthony was unsure ("technically, there is a projectE (embeddings-rs, though I'm not sure yet if this is a reflow2 project)"). MEASURED: the `.reflow2` directory EXISTS and `describe_designs` reports `state: absent` — "no design here." So it is OPTED IN AND EMPTY: somebody created the directory and no design was ever started. That is a distinct state from both "is a reflow2 project" and "is not one", and reflow2 reports it precisely because opening the store to find out would MINT an identity and make the answer true by asking.

⚠️ AND STORYFLOW ALREADY DECLARES `ifc:embeddings_api` ("Embeddings REST API"), so D depends on an embeddings service that has no design at all. Whether that service IS embeddings-rs is still not established.

=== 🔴 THREE IDENTITY CONVENTIONS ACROSS FOUR GRAPHS, AND ONE OUTRIGHT COLLISION ===

- `dynograph-foundation` — graph_id equals the label. The convention working.
- `flo2` — graph_id is a MINTED HASH `1a97fc1f1de4d5d2`, label `flo2`. Different convention, and it is the one `minted` origin among four.
- **`dev_storyflow` carries graph_id `reflow2` — THE SAME ID AS REFLOW2 ITSELF.** Two distinct designs, one id.

⇒ This is exactly the Contributor-fork defect found earlier today (`ctr:anthony` / `who:ajs`) ONE LEVEL UP: **the field whose entire purpose is identity is the one nothing checks for duplicate identity.** It is also `rule:no-foreclosure` clause (5) in the field. Every cross-project mechanism in `dec:idea-gap-flows-to-the-dependency` and `dec:idea-a-change-upstream-reaches-the-sibling-that-never-asked` runs through composition, and **composition cannot tell B's nodes from D's by graph_id.** `label` distinguishes them; the id does not.

=== ⚠️⚠️ THE PROJECT AT THE BOTTOM OF THE STACK HAS THE STALEST DESIGN ===

**dynograph-foundation's graph was written by reflow2 0.16.0 and has not moved since — roughly ELEVEN releases behind the 0.27.0 cut today.** Its stamp holds 56 edge types and 28 node types against the current 61 and 29. It predates `OWNED_BY`, `GATED_ON`, `HAS_READINESS`, `SCHEDULED_FOR`, `CALIBRATED_AGAINST` and the whole `ReadinessAssessment` type.

THE SHAPE IS THE FINDING: **A is what B, C and D all rest on, and A is the least-maintained design of the four.** Every consumer's graph is current; the thing they depend on is a year of releases behind in design terms. And the practical consequence bites immediately on the question Anthony asked — filing a proposed requirement INTO A's graph with a 0.27.0 binary will MOVE A'S STAMP from 0.16.0 to 0.27.0, which is a real and irreversible side effect of what looks like a read-mostly act of filing an issue.

BOUND: `describe_designs` deliberately reports NO node counts, because counting means opening, and opening mints an identity where there is none. So this census says what each design IS, never how big it is. D's and A's contents are known here only from their committed exports, not their live stores.
